cohort: The study included 120 pregnant women undergoing Caesarean section surgery, divided into two groups receiving either general or spinal anesthesia.
finding: Spinal anesthesia is associated with significantly higher incidences of intraoperative hypotension and postoperative headaches and backaches compared to general anesthesia during Caesarean section surgeries.
mod_finding: The findings indicate that for Caesarean sections, spinal anesthesia is linked to a higher incidence of intraoperative hypotension and postoperative headaches and backaches compared to general anesthesia.
